correctness.rationale: For an edge connecting different coalitions, positive internal degree and ambient degree \(\leq2\) force each endpoint to have precisely one inside and one outside neighbor. The two no-deviation inequalities therefore reduce exactly to a difference of coalition sizes at most one. Vertices without inside neighbors can join a neighbor to improve, and under the two conditions every remaining deviation either has payoff zero or is constrained by that edge inequality. For cycles, each disconnected coalition arc and each gap contain at least two vertices, proving \(n\geq4t\). Alternating two-vertex runs with balanced residual vertices attain \(t=\lfloor n/4\rfloor\); \(n=8\) forces two repeated AABB patterns. A separate exact-integer checker independently computes unilateral incentives on 172620 small unrestricted partitions and finds no contradictions; finite checks do not prove the general theorem.

value.rationale: Nash stability of every coalition structure, not just existence of a favorable equilibrium, can be certified in linear time for all simple symmetric graphs of maximum degree two and no isolated agents. The exact geographical fragmentation extremum \(\lfloor n/4\rfloor\) and first eight-cycle multiplicity expose a structural possibility that grand-coalition/path welfare optimizations do not describe. This is a natural all-size coalition-formation invariant with a tight constructive boundary, not a one-off small-instance calculation.
